title: Functionalists at Work
welcome_lead: Apply Parsons, Murdock and AGIL to family, education and crime — the institutions exam questions love.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying functionalism to family, education and crime, with AGIL.
final_note: Pair every institution with the function it performs — that locks in AO2 marks.

concepts.def: Functionalist who saw family doing four key roles.
Linked family and school to industrial society needs.
First norms learned in the family.
Parsons: family relaxes adults after work.
Merton: an institution's intended useful role.

walkthroughs.body_html: Murdock studied 250 societies in 1949 and claimed the family always performs four roles: sexual, reproductive, economic and educational. Critics say his sample ignored variety.
Parsons argued the nuclear family is the best 'fit' for industrial society: small and mobile. It performs primary socialisation and stabilisation of adult personalities (the warm-bath theory).
Parsons claimed every system meets four needs: Adaptation (economy), Goal-attainment (politics), Integration (law), Latency (family, religion). This is the AGIL scheme.
